If the pronoun refers to (man, "whoever"), the lam carries its meaning; or it refers to both meanings together, so the pronoun refers to mankind in general, and the lam has a general figurative meaning covering both senses. ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾ — that is, His threat, or His saying to the angels: ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together."﴾ — that is, from among their disobedient ones, all together, or from both of them all together, not from only one of them.

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 11, verse 120:**

﴿And each﴾, i.e., each report. The *tanwin* (nunation, the "n" sound at the end of the word, here *kullan*) stands as a substitute (*ʿiwaḍ*) for the omitted genitive complement. ﴿We relate to you﴾, we inform you of it. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿of the reports of the messengers﴾, is an explanation (*bayan*) of *kullan*. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿with which We strengthen your heart﴾, is a substitute (*badal*) for it. The more apparent view is that the omitted genitive complement of *kullan* is the absolute object (*al-mafʿul al-mutlaq*) of *naquṣṣu* (we relate), meaning: each act of relating, i.e., each of its methods, We relate to you of the reports of the messengers.

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿with which We strengthen your heart﴾, is the object (*mafʿul*) of *naquṣṣu*. Its purpose is to draw attention to the fact that the aim of relating these reports is to increase his certainty, peace be upon him, to calm his heart, and to steady his soul in conveying the message and bearing the harm of the disbelievers, by knowing the details of the circumstances of the earlier nations in their persistence in misguidance, and what the messengers encountered from them of the hardships they endured.

﴿And there has come to you in this﴾ surah, or in the reports related to you, ﴿the truth﴾ from which there is no escape, ﴿and an admonition and a reminder for the believers﴾. That is, it combines being truth in itself with being an admonition and a reminder for the believers. Because the first attribute is a state (*ḥal*) of it in itself, it is defined with the article (*al-*), unlike what it is described as in relation to something else. The fronting of the adverbial phrase, namely *fi hadhihi* (in this), before the subject is because the aim is to explain the benefits of the surah, or of the reports related in it, and its inclusion of the detailed benefits mentioned, not to state that these are in it and not in anything else. Also, when something that should be placed first is delayed, the soul remains anticipating it, so it settles in it more deeply when it arrives. And also, in the delayed element there is a kind of length, which placing it first would disrupt the harmonious correspondence of the parts of the noble composition. (p-249)

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 11, verse 121:

﴿And say to those who do not believe﴾ in this truth, and who do not take admonition from it nor remember it. ﴿Act according to your station﴾ according to your condition and your course, which is non-belief. ﴿Indeed, we are acting﴾ according to our condition, which is belief in it, taking admonition from it, and remembering it.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 11, verse 122:

﴿And wait﴾ for the calamities [to befall us], ﴿indeed we are waiting﴾ for what will befall you, something like what befell your likes among the disbelievers.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 11, verse 123:

﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him the whole matter is returned.﴾ So your affair and theirs will inevitably return to Him. It is also read in the active voice, from rajaʿa (rujuʿan): "yarji'u" [the verb form is read as active]. ﴿So worship Him and put your trust in Him.﴾ For He is sufficient for you. The fa' (fa, "so") indicates the sequence of the command to worship and to trust in Him upon the fact that the return of all matters is to Allah the Exalted. The delay of the command to trust (tawakkul) after the command to worship indicates that trust is of no benefit without worship. ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what they do.﴾ So He will recompense them according to what it requires. It is also read as "taʿmalūna" (you [plural] do), by way of addressing the one addressed predominantly, i.e., you and they together, so He will recompense each of you and them according to what is deserved.

From the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surah Hud will be given the reward of ten good deeds for each of the prophets mentioned in it who affirmed each one of the prophets (peace be upon them), and for the number of those who denied them, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be among the blessed, by the grace of Allah, glorified and exalted is He."
